newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq's Aziz sees chief of oil delegation from China.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's Aziz sees chief of oil delegation from China.

text.p: Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz has praised China for wanting U.N. trade sanctions on Baghdad lifted, the official Iraqi News Agency said on Wednesday.

INA said Aziz met Zhou Yong-Kang, who is chairman of the Chinese National Petroleum Corporation and in Baghdad leading a large technical delegation, and told him that Iraq was keen to expand bilateral ties.
"The deputy premier praised China's principled and fair stands in supporting Iraq's legitimate right to have the unfair embargo imposed on it removed," INA said.
Zhou arrived in Baghdad on Sunday and was expected to sign an oil contract to develop the billion-barrel Ahdab oil field in southern Iraq.
Zhou and his delegation visited Ahdab on Tuesday. He also met Vice-President Taha Yassin Ramadan.
"Oil cooperation is a clear indication of China's desire to develop relations with Iraq and that China will exert all efforts to have the embargo removed," INA quoted Zhou as saying.
China's foreign minister last month said Beijing wanted to see an end to U.N. sanctions against Iraq as soon as possible.

Iraq is under U.N. trade sanctions for invading Kuwait in 1990. The U.N. partially eased the oil ban by allowing Iraq limited exports of $2 billion in six months. The deal expires on June 7 but is expected to extended for another six months.
Oil officials say the Chinese are also interested in the development of the prized Halfaya field in the south.
